title: FUNAAB curriculum research manifest
scope: Catalogue of all programmes in the eight supplied FUNAAB research reports. Programme names, synopses, URLs, confidence levels, and gaps are preserved without filling missing evidence.

domains.source_notes: The report contains the detailed Markdown research and PDF inventory. Research prioritized official FUNAAB admission, college, department, postgraduate, NUC approval, course, and PDF sources. The official admission page controls the exact 23-programme set. Individual course-unit listings and postgraduate specializations were explicitly distinguished from programme-level descriptions. No secondary student guide was needed. Main caveat: FUNAAB does not expose a single current public undergraduate handbook for all 23 programmes; Water Sanitation and Hygiene remains low confidence because only the official admission listing was found.

courses.name: Agriculture
courses.synopsis: Broad Bachelor of Agriculture programme introducing crop and livestock production, soil and natural-resource management, allied agricultural disciplines, and practical farm experience.
gaps: No current public complete undergraduate handbook or course-unit syllabus located.

courses.name: Agricultural Administration
courses.synopsis: Agriculture-focused administration and leadership oriented toward economic agricultural production, policy, organization, management, and practical agricultural operations; one of COLAMRUD's B.Agric options.
gaps: Current semester-by-semester curriculum not publicly located.

courses.name: Agricultural Economics and Farm Management
courses.synopsis: Applies economics and management to agricultural production, processing, storage, marketing, farm decisions, and rural enterprise; an official COLAMRUD B.Agric option.
gaps: Exact undergraduate course sequence and learning outcomes unavailable publicly.

courses.name: Agricultural Extension and Rural Development
courses.synopsis: Develops capacity to communicate agricultural knowledge and support rural development through extension teaching, communication, community development, social processes, programme planning, and supervision. The official course page is a course-unit list, not a full programme syllabus.
gaps: Current programme handbook, assessment structure, and complete syllabus not located.

courses.name: Animal Breeding and Genetics
courses.synopsis: Focuses on genetic improvement of farm animals and principles used to select, breed, and manage productive livestock populations.
gaps: No current undergraduate curriculum or detailed learning outcomes located.

courses.name: Animal Nutrition
courses.synopsis: Covers feeds, feeding, nutrient use, and diet formulation for livestock; FUNAAB describes the department as concerned with feeds and feeding of all classes of animals.
gaps: No current public undergraduate course handbook located.

courses.name: Animal Physiology
courses.synopsis: Examines how animal bodies function, with application to animal production and health.
gaps: Current undergraduate option structure and course sequence not stated publicly.

courses.name: Animal Production and Health
courses.synopsis: Integrates livestock production with animal health to support efficient and healthy production of livestock and livestock products.
gaps: Detailed production systems, species coverage, and current curriculum not exposed.

courses.name: Aquaculture and Fisheries Management
courses.synopsis: Covers aquatic animal production and fisheries-resource management, including aquaculture, fisheries management, fish nutrition, and fish pathology as documented in FUNAAB postgraduate areas. Undergraduate handbook and current course details were not located; postgraduate specializations are not treated as undergraduate units.
gaps: Undergraduate handbook and current course details not located; postgraduate specializations are not treated as undergraduate units.

courses.name: Climate Science and Agricultural Meteorology
courses.synopsis: Applies climate science, climatology, meteorology, and climate analysis to agriculture, including effects on crops, animals, forestry, aquaculture, farm planning, weather forecasting, and climate-related agricultural losses.
gaps: Complete undergraduate curriculum not published on the approval page.

courses.name: Crop Protection
courses.synopsis: Addresses protection of crops from pests, diseases, weeds, and related production losses; postgraduate subject areas include virology, nematology, entomology, pathology, and weed science.
gaps: Detailed prospectus is older; current undergraduate syllabus not located.

courses.name: Environmental Management and Toxicology
courses.synopsis: Trains environmental personnel in surveillance, monitoring, management, resource depletion, recycling, reuse, and impacts of science and technology, with toxicology as an advanced area.
gaps: Page uses both Environmental Management and Environmental Resources Management wording; current curriculum unavailable.

courses.name: Forest Resource Management
courses.synopsis: Manages forest resources through silviculture, forest ecology and conservation, forest economics, biometrics/remote sensing, wood science, and related resource-use practice.
gaps: Current B.Sc. course handbook not located.

courses.name: Geology
courses.synopsis: Provides geological knowledge and practical skills for mineral, water, petroleum, engineering, environmental, and geo-hazard applications, including contaminated soil and water remediation.
gaps: Geology is adjacent to, rather than directly a crop/animal-production discipline; no public curriculum PDF located.

courses.name: Horticulture
courses.synopsis: Trains students in production, improvement, storage, handling, and marketing of horticultural crops.
gaps: Current course units and programme handbook not located.

courses.name: Hydrology and Water Resources Management
courses.synopsis: Applies hydrology and water-resource principles to water exploration, extraction, quality, distribution, drainage-basin development, and domestic, agricultural, and industrial use.
gaps: The approval title and department title are related but not identical; no curriculum crosswalk located.

courses.name: Pasture and Range Management
courses.synopsis: Focuses on pasture production and utilization, forage resources, and range management for livestock systems.
gaps: Current undergraduate handbook and detailed learning outcomes not located.

courses.name: Plant Breeding and Seed Technology
courses.synopsis: Covers improvement of crop varieties and seed technology, including plant breeding and production and management of quality seed.
gaps: Current undergraduate curriculum and detailed seed-quality units not located.

courses.name: Plant Physiology and Crop Production
courses.synopsis: Integrates plant function with crop production; FUNAAB identifies crop physiology, crop ecology, and crop production as related postgraduate areas.
gaps: Current undergraduate course-unit details not located.

courses.name: Soil Science and Land Management
courses.synopsis: Applies soil science and land management to sustainable food production, soil fertility, soil-water conservation, soil degradation, pollution prevention, land use, and environmental protection.
gaps: Detailed department page is historical in parts; current complete curriculum not located.

courses.name: Water Resources Management and Agro-meteorology
courses.synopsis: Trains students in water-resource exploration, quality monitoring, distribution, hydrology, climatology, meteorology, agricultural weather forecasting, and climate impacts on crops, animals, forestry, and aquaculture.
gaps: Do not merge this listed programme with Hydrology and Water Resources Management without a current official curriculum crosswalk.

courses.name: Wildlife and Eco-tourism Management
courses.synopsis: Combines wildlife management, ecology and conservation, domestication and production, park planning, recreation, interpretation, and eco-tourism-oriented resource use.
gaps: Department page is titled Forestry and Wildlife Management and lacks a dedicated current Eco-tourism curriculum.

courses.name: Water Sanitation and Hygiene
courses.synopsis: Officially listed by FUNAAB, but no programme-level official description or curriculum was located. The safe catalogue synopsis is limited to the title-level domain of water, sanitation, hygiene, and related public/environmental health practice.
gaps: No official programme page, handbook, curriculum, or public PDF found; do not infer detailed course content from the title.

domains.source_notes: The detailed Markdown report includes a source-linked synopsis table, PDF inventory, evidence hierarchy, and explicit distinction between programme-level descriptions and individual course-unit materials. Official FUNAAB sources were prioritised; no secondary student guides were needed. Public descriptions for newly approved Biotechnology, Public Health, and Science Laboratory Technology are intentionally conservative because substantive undergraduate curricula were not publicly located.

courses.name: Biochemistry
courses.synopsis: A four-year B.Sc. programme centred on the chemistry of life, from microorganisms to humans, with relevance to industry, medicine, and agriculture and emphasis on research, communication, entrepreneurship, problem-solving, lifelong learning, and information technology.
gaps: No complete current undergraduate course grid or unit-by-unit syllabus was located; the postgraduate PDF is not undergraduate curriculum evidence.

courses.name: Biotechnology
courses.synopsis: A newly approved full-time B.Sc. programme commencing in the 2026/2027 session. FUNAAB confirms the degree and approval and lists it with a 190 minimum acceptable UTME score; no fuller public curriculum description was located.
gaps: No substantive undergraduate department page, curriculum handbook, learning outcomes, or programme syllabus was located. A single open-courseware Biotechnology lecture cannot represent the programme curriculum.

courses.name: Microbiology
courses.synopsis: A four-year B.Sc. programme, or three years by Direct Entry, studying bacteria, algae, protozoa, fungi, and viruses across ecology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, and disease relationships. FUNAAB highlights applications in food, breweries, pharmaceuticals, medicine, agriculture, water works, healthcare laboratories, forensics, biodegradation, and environmental monitoring.
gaps: No complete current undergraduate course handbook was located; the Food Microbiology PDF is an individual course-unit document, not a programme syllabus.

courses.name: Public Health
courses.synopsis: A newly approved full-time B.Sc. programme commencing in 2026/2027. FUNAAB lists it under Biological Science with a 190 minimum acceptable UTME score and confirms NUC approval. Available official evidence establishes the programme but not its detailed subject areas or course sequence.
gaps: No substantive undergraduate Public Health department page, curriculum, learning outcomes, or course-unit syllabi was located. Veterinary Public Health sources were excluded because they describe a different field.

courses.name: Pure and Applied Botany
courses.synopsis: A B.Sc. programme providing broad botanical knowledge and practical skills, with application to theoretical and practical problems and to industrial, economic, environmental, technological, and social development. Training includes lectures, practicals, tutorials, industrial training, field trips, computer training, and research; normal duration is four years from 100 level or three by Direct Entry.
gaps: No complete current course-by-semester curriculum was located; OpenCourseware items are individual course resources only.

courses.name: Pure and Applied Zoology
courses.synopsis: A B.Sc. Zoology programme focused on animals, including physiology, anatomy, genetics, and ecology, with relevance to agriculture, human and animal public health, disease and pest control, environmental work, GIS mapping, and small-animal breeding. Training includes lectures, laboratory work, industrial training, field trips, and research; the department states four years for UME entry, three for eligible Direct Entry, and at least 120 graduation units including 60 departmental units.
gaps: The departmental profile is detailed but is not a current semester-by-semester handbook; courseware items are not the complete curriculum.

courses.name: Science Laboratory Technology
courses.synopsis: A newly approved full-time B.Sc. programme commencing in 2026/2027. FUNAAB confirms the degree and NUC approval and lists “Science Lab Technology” with a 190 minimum acceptable UTME score; the public evidence does not support a more detailed curriculum synopsis without speculation.
gaps: No substantive undergraduate department page, course handbook, programme learning outcomes, or course-unit syllabi was located. Legacy admission references do not establish the new B.Sc. curriculum.

domains.source_notes: Research used official FUNAAB department/college pages, the official 2026/2027 admission programme listing, the official NUC approval announcement, and official FUNAAB-hosted PDFs. No secondary student guides were needed. The report includes a PDF inventory and explicitly distinguishes programme-level descriptions from individual course-unit materials. Current programme-specific curricula and syllabi were not publicly located, so exact modules, sequencing, credits, tools and languages should not be inferred.

courses.name: Computer Science
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB describes a broad theory-and-practice computer science programme covering programming for real-life problems, computing services, software application development, basic networking and hardware, and preparation for postgraduate study and research.
gaps: No current official curriculum, semester course map, credit structure, or individual course-unit syllabi located.
The historical Computer Science course list is legacy material and was not treated as a current curriculum.

courses.name: Cyber Security
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB frames Cyber Security around protecting digital assets, critical infrastructure and business ecosystems. Official objectives include cybersecurity foundations, threat/risk analysis, cyber-fraud prevention, security code and agents, digital forensics, cryptography, professional practice and lifelong learning; the rationale also names threat intelligence, threat hunting, deep/dark-web security, AI cyber defence and surveillance.
gaps: No official public curriculum, course map, credit structure or course-unit syllabi located.

courses.name: Data Science
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB’s Data Science programme aims to reveal useful knowledge from large data stores for decision-making and organizational value. Its official objectives cover computationally intensive problem solving, information extraction, data engineering, big data, analytics and integration of data-driven IT solutions with business processes; the rationale highlights hands-on analytics, machine learning, AI and deep learning.
gaps: No current official curriculum, course map, credit structure or course-unit syllabi located; languages, platforms and assessment formats are unspecified.

courses.name: Information Communication Technology
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB presents ICT as preparation for professional development and seamless ICT integration for productivity. Objectives cover foundational ICT concepts, ICT acquisition/disposal, professional practice, emerging technologies and practical utilization; the rationale identifies hands-on work in web applications, multimedia, document processing, mobile computing and internet communications, with ICT commercialisation and technology management career directions.
gaps: No current public curriculum, handbook or individual ICT course syllabi located; the ICT Policy is institutional context, not a programme curriculum.

courses.name: Information Systems
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB focuses Information Systems on developing and maintaining quality systems at scale for organizations while satisfying functional and non-functional requirements within time and budget. Objectives include computing foundations, requirements analysis, system design and architecture, metrics, verification/validation, programming, secure robust systems and management of complex critical systems.
gaps: No detailed Information Systems curriculum, course map, credit structure or course-unit syllabi located; the public objectives closely parallel Software Engineering and do not establish distinctive modules.

courses.name: Information Technology
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB positions IT around solving needs through IT solutions, information assurance and security, abstraction/modeling and professional standards. Objectives cover IT foundations, data management, practical problem solving, computing and communications, infrastructure quality, employment and further study; the rationale highlights web technologies, network servers/infrastructure, mobile/pervasive computing and mobile/web application development.
gaps: No current official curriculum, course-unit syllabi, credit structure or detailed infrastructure laboratory specification located.

courses.name: Software Engineering
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB’s Software Engineering programme targets development and maintenance of quality software systems at scale that meet functional and non-functional requirements within time and budget. Official objectives include computing foundations, requirements analysis, design and architecture, metrics, verification/validation, software processes, multi-language programming, secure robust systems, complex-system management, ethics and self-employment.
gaps: No current official Software Engineering curriculum, semester sequence, credit structure or course-unit syllabi located.

domains.source_notes: Detailed Markdown report completed with official FUNAAB admission, college, departmental, postgraduate, and PDF links. Current admission confirms all six listed programmes. Official programme-level pages support Chemistry, Mathematics, Physics, and Statistics; Geophysics and Industrial Chemistry have verified programme listings but significant undergraduate-description gaps. No secondary student guides were used. The report explicitly distinguishes programme-level descriptions from course-unit syllabi and includes a PDF inventory.

courses.name: Chemistry
courses.synopsis: A four-year B.Sc. programme developing broad theoretical and practical chemistry knowledge, understanding of chemical principles and applications, and adaptable skills for research, tertiary teaching, chemical/manufacturing industry, or self-employment. The official page states that students undertake a six-month industrial attachment beginning at the start of second semester in Year 3.
gaps: No current complete undergraduate course-by-course handbook or semester curriculum PDF was located.
The postgraduate prospectus is historical/postgraduate context, not a B.Sc. syllabus.

courses.name: Geophysics
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB officially lists Geophysics under Physical Science admissions. The public undergraduate pages reviewed do not provide a standalone B.Sc. Geophysics philosophy, objectives, duration, or course structure. FUNAAB separately lists Solid Earth Physics/Geophysics as a postgraduate field.
gaps: No current standalone undergraduate Geophysics programme page or curriculum was located.
Geophysics is absent from the five-department list on the COLPHYS page; administrative home needs confirmation.
Do not infer Geophysics content from the Geology page.

courses.name: Industrial Chemistry
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB officially lists Industrial Chemistry under Physical Science admissions and lists Industrial Chemistry among its postgraduate fields. The public undergraduate material reviewed does not provide a distinct B.Sc. Industrial Chemistry synopsis, objectives, industrial-training rules, or course list separate from Chemistry.
gaps: No distinct current undergraduate Industrial Chemistry programme page or complete curriculum was located.
Chemistry departmental claims must not be presented as a verified Industrial Chemistry syllabus.

courses.name: Mathematics
courses.synopsis: A B.Sc. (Hons) programme designed to provide broad mathematical knowledge and allow development toward Pure or Applied Mathematics. Official objectives emphasize rigorous and logical reasoning, analytical thinking, mathematical techniques for scientific and technological problems, research preparation, service instruction, and applications in teaching, finance, software development, business, and system analysis.
gaps: The department says a curriculum exists but no complete current course inventory or handbook PDF was located.
Employment fields named on the page are broad outcomes, not proof of formal specializations.

courses.name: Physics
courses.synopsis: A single-honours B.Sc. programme intended to provide a broad and balanced foundation in Physics, practical skills, appreciation of applications, theoretical and practical problem-solving ability, transferable skills, and preparation for research, industrial applications, and further multidisciplinary study.
gaps: No complete current undergraduate Physics course list or handbook PDF was located.
The postgraduate prospectus supports postgraduate fields only and is not an undergraduate syllabus.

courses.name: Statistics
courses.synopsis: A B.Sc. programme providing broad knowledge of statistical theory and application across physical and life sciences, engineering, education, and social sciences. Objectives include professional statistical problem-solving, statistical methods for scientific/technological research and national planning, academic development, service teaching, and consultancy-oriented employment. The official page also states graduation requirements including completion of required University, College/Department core, and elective courses and a minimum CGPA of 1.0.
gaps: No complete current undergraduate Statistics course list, credit structure, or handbook PDF was located.
Graduation rules do not identify individual units or semester placement.

domains.source_notes: Detailed 107-line Markdown report created and verified at the requested path. Research prioritized official FUNAAB college, departmental, admissions, course-list, course-synopsis, and public PDF sources. The report includes a PDF inventory, numeric reference definitions, programme-versus-course-unit distinctions, confidence ratings, and explicit gaps. No secondary student guides were needed.

courses.name: Clothing & Textile Design
courses.synopsis: An applied design and production pathway focused on clothing construction, textile design and production, pattern drafting, fashion drawing, interior decoration/design, tailoring, and related consultancy or enterprise practice. FUNAAB documents Clothing and Textiles primarily as an option/broad discipline within Home Science and Management, while its 2026 admissions page lists Clothing & Textile Design separately.
gaps: No standalone current undergraduate Clothing & Textile Design department page, complete curriculum handbook, degree map, credit structure, or programme-level learning-outcomes document was found.
The HSM course list and HSM 410 PDF are supporting course/unit evidence and must not be treated as proof of the complete separate degree curriculum.

courses.name: Food Science and Technology
courses.synopsis: A multidisciplinary science-and-engineering programme concerned with food raw materials, composition, quality, processing, preservation, storage, packaging, and food-industry systems. FUNAAB describes broad preparation in basic sciences, engineering applications, food processing and preservation, with scope for later specialization and careers in agro-industry, government, and food-security work.
gaps: No current consolidated undergraduate curriculum/credit map or single programme handbook was located.
The course synopsis page describes individual course units, not the programme specification.

courses.name: Home Science and Management
courses.synopsis: A broad human-ecology and family-resource programme concerned with improving family quality of life through effective use of human and material resources. FUNAAB describes instruction in child development and family studies, clothing and textiles, home science extension, household and institutional resource management, laboratory and field work, workshops, and industrial training.
gaps: The official page does not provide a complete current degree curriculum, course credits, or detailed learning outcomes for every option.

courses.name: Hospitality and Tourism
courses.synopsis: An interdisciplinary service-management programme integrating catering/foodservice, hotel and hospitality operations, food composition and preparation, food safety and quality assurance, marketing and consumer education, tourism development and transportation services, tourism law, and tourist management. FUNAAB frames it as preparation for entrepreneurial, leadership, operational, research, and service roles.
gaps: The official page uses both Hospitality and Tourism and older Foodservice and Tourism terminology.
No complete current course-by-course undergraduate handbook or degree map was located.

courses.name: Nutrition and Dietetics
courses.synopsis: A human-nutrition and clinical/community dietetics programme covering nutrients and metabolism, nutrition assessment, public-health and community nutrition, nutrition research, nutrition in disease, clinical nutrition, diet therapy, foodservice management, nutrition education, and diet planning. FUNAAB emphasizes laboratory, field, workshop, and applied practice for health, foodservice, government, and community settings.
gaps: No current consolidated undergraduate curriculum handbook, degree map, or credit structure was located.
The synopsis and NTD 313 PDF are course-unit sources and must not be treated as the full programme specification.

Course synopsis does not establish current sequencing, prerequisites or completeness

courses.name: Civil Engineering
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB's programme develops skilled, creative and employable civil engineers grounded in fundamentals and industrial exposure, able to apply engineering judgment and appropriate technology to civil-engineering and agricultural problems, with supervised practical training and site exposure.
gaps: No current undergraduate curriculum/handbook PDF located
Course synopsis is unit-level and not a complete current programme map

courses.name: Electrical and Electronics Engineering
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB's programme combines electrical/electronics theory and practice across power systems, renewable energy, electronics, automatic control, communications and computer applications, preparing students for engineering problem-solving, ICT development, agricultural services and power, telecommunications and industrial work.
gaps: No current undergraduate curriculum/handbook PDF located
Course synopsis does not establish current course sequencing or complete unit inventory

courses.name: Mechanical Engineering
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB's programme focuses on analysis, design and synthesis of prime movers, engines, turbines, refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment, machine tools, material-handling and industrial production systems and manufacturing robots, with graduate capabilities in drawings, practical problem-solving, machinery operation/maintenance and engineering management.

MCE 509 PDF is an individual dated lecture note, not a degree curriculum

courses.name: Mechatronic Engineering
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB's Mechatronics programme develops engineers for industrialization and automation, covering design of components, machines, equipment and systems; product and production development; complex-system installation and maintenance; local adaptation of technology; professional judgment and multidisciplinary teamwork. Official unit synopses span CAD/CAM/CNC, control, instrumentation, computer hardware, power electronics, robotics, PLC/process automation, embedded systems and renewable energy.
gaps: No current undergraduate curriculum/handbook PDF located
Legacy department page has mechanical-engineering wording; current section page is preferred

domains.source_notes: Research used official FUNAAB College, departmental, course-synopsis, Postgraduate School, and admission sources. No secondary student guide was needed. The report distinguishes programme-level descriptions from individual course-unit syllabi and includes a direct-PDF inventory. The only directly relevant official programme PDF located was the 2026 admission-requirements document; the other listed PDFs are individual lecture/open-courseware resources, not complete curriculum documents.

courses.name: Veterinary Medicine
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB’s Veterinary Medicine programme is a six-year professional Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) degree for students admitted at 100 level, comprising 12 semesters: a two-semester pre-professional phase and a ten-semester professional phase from 200–600 level. The professional phase includes three semesters of pre-clinical study, three semesters of para-clinical study, and four semesters of clinical study. The College states that the programme prepares students for animal health, livestock production, public health, research, teaching, and veterinary practice. Professional-phase courses are compulsory, and students must complete at least six months of approved Field Study under veterinary-surgeon supervision and submit a report. The award is the unclassified Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM). The official course-synopsis page provides selected individual unit descriptions, including introductory veterinary medicine, general medicine, food-animal medicine, avian medicine, companion/laboratory-animal medicine, wildlife and fisheries medicine, clinical medicine, surgery, anaesthesia, intensive care, lameness, diagnostic imaging, and practical surgery; these are course-unit synopses and are not presented as an exhaustive programme curriculum.
gaps: No complete current public semester-by-semester DVM curriculum handbook was located.
The official course-synopsis page is selective and does not provide every course code, semester, prerequisite, learning outcome, or assessment method.
FUNAAB pages use inconsistent department counts and grouped department labels; this does not affect the verified programme-level structure.
Admission requirements may change by admission cycle; the linked 2026 PDF should be checked before operational use.
Postgraduate M.V.Sc and Ph.D. Veterinary Medicine specializations were found but are out of scope for this undergraduate programme record.

courses.name: Accounting
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB describes Accounting as preparing efficient and effective accounting scholars and practitioners, with emphasis on public/private-sector relevance, global competitiveness, professional and teaching careers, ethics, socio-economic/environmental awareness, teamwork and leadership. Programme-level summary only; no course-unit claims.
gaps: No complete official Accounting curriculum, handbook, or unit-by-unit syllabus located.

courses.name: Banking and Finance
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB frames Banking and Finance around finance concepts and theories for complex financial/economic issues and better decisions by government, corporations and individuals. It stresses ethical financial-services conduct, self-reliance, professional and leadership preparation, further study, teamwork and enterprise-building.
gaps: The BFN PDF is an individual course-unit document, not a full curriculum; no complete official handbook found.

courses.name: Business Administration
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB combines theoretical and practical management knowledge with self-reliance and the ability to understand, exploit and potentially change the environment through management theories and techniques. Objectives include organisational problem analysis, scientific decision tools, environmental awareness, leadership/interpersonal skills, entrepreneurship, manager/teacher/researcher preparation and Nigerian-context management research.
gaps: No complete official curriculum, course handbook or unit syllabi located.

courses.name: Cooperative Studies
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB’s current admissions list confirms Cooperative Studies within the Entrepreneurial and Development Studies grouping, with a 160 UTME screening mark. The reviewed official college page supplies only broad college-level themes of theoretical/practical knowledge, self-reliance, innovation and management/development; no Cooperative Studies-specific content is stated, so no further subject synopsis is inferred.
gaps: No official Cooperative Studies department page, programme objectives, curriculum, handbook or course syllabi located.

courses.name: Development Studies
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB’s admissions list confirms Development Studies within the Entrepreneurial and Development Studies grouping, with a 160 UTME screening mark. The college history links its renaming/expansion to programmes aligned with Development Studies, but the reviewed official sources do not provide programme-specific coverage, outcomes or course structure; no content is invented.
gaps: No official Development Studies department page, programme-specific objectives, curriculum, handbook or course syllabi located.

courses.name: Economics
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB presents Economics as developing theoretical and practical knowledge for work in academia, industry and public-sector settings nationally and internationally. Its objective is strong foundations in economic theory, tools of economic analysis, and useful knowledge/skills for contemporary economic issues, policy and society; the department also emphasizes research, teaching, learning and outreach toward sustainable development.
gaps: No complete official Economics curriculum or undergraduate handbook located; Agricultural Economics course synopsis was not treated as this programme’s curriculum.

courses.name: Entrepreneurial Studies
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB describes Entrepreneurial Studies as developing innovative, creative and entrepreneurial personalities for leadership in industry, government and non-profits. Objectives include entrepreneurial knowledge/zeal, viable globally competitive enterprises, opportunity recognition, venture growth, productive culture, mentoring/advisory engagement, and analytical skills in problem solving, negotiation, conflict resolution, marketing, leadership, interpersonal relations and financial management.
gaps: No complete official curriculum or course handbook located.

courses.name: Library and Information Science
courses.synopsis: FUNAAB describes Library and Information Science as training professionals who develop/apply relevant technologies and information, manage information in all formats, and work in physical/virtual libraries and related organisations. Objectives include library/documentation professionalism, theoretical and practical competence, inquiry/creativity, adaptability and use of new communication technologies; identified fields include libraries, ICT industries, archives, museums, information centres and public establishments.
gaps: No complete official Library and Information Science curriculum or handbook located; FUNAAB uses B.LIS in the NUC announcement and Library and Information Science in the later admissions list, likely naming variants.
